{{short description|None}}

{{Update|date=October 2018}}
{{China divisions by}}

Sex-based statistics regarding the rate of '''infant mortality by administrative divisions in the People's Republic of China''' have been collected.  Disparity in rates of female [[infant mortality]] by Chinese administrative divisions has been noted in public health statistics since the [[Third National Population Census of the People's Republic of China|first modern Chinese census]] in 1982 which showed significantly higher rates of female infant mortality.<ref name="fudanstudy">{{cite journal|last1=Cao|first1=Meng|last2=Lei|first2=Peng|last3=Wu|first3=Zhuochun|title=Gender Difference of Infant Mortality and its Disparity among Provinces in China|journal=Chinese Journal of Health Statistics|date=April 2013|volume=30|issue=2|pages=162–166|url=http://xueshu.baidu.com/s?wd=paperuri%3A%28524649d3be57f8042703c2bf3292917f%29&filter=sc_long_sign&tn=SE_xueshusource_2kduw22v&sc_vurl=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.docin.com%2Fp-1610574489.html&ie=utf-8&sc_us=17348083949130733610}}</ref> Already abnormal female infant mortality deteriorated further in censuses held in 1989 and 2000.<ref name="fudanstudy"/>

==Census data==
===2010===
The infant mortality rates by administrative division from the [[Sixth National Population Census of the People's Republic of China|6th National Population Census]] held in 2010 are adjusted upwards according to a methodology by the authors Professors Hong Rongqing and Zeng Xianxin of [[Capital University of Economics and Business]] in "Infant Mortality Reported in the 2010 Census: Bias and Adjustment", published in ''Population Research'' in March 2013.<ref name="populationresearch">{{cite journal|last1=Hong|first1=Rongqing|last2=Zeng|first2=Xianxin|title=Infant Mortality Reported in the 2010 Census: Bias and Adjustment|journal=Population Research|date=March 2013|volume=37|url=http://rkyj.ruc.edu.cn/EN/abstract/abstract3213.shtml}}</ref> The authors estimate that the infant mortality rate from the 6th Census is severely underreported by about 78%.<ref name="populationresearch"/> Undereporting of the infant mortality rate in the 6th Census is also the conclusion in a note analyzing the 6th Census by the China offices of [[UNICEF]] and [[UNFPA]].<ref name="un">{{cite web|title=What Census Data Can Tell Us About Children in China Facts and Figures 2013|url=http://www.unicef.cn/en/uploadfile/2013/1216/20131216111141945.pdf|website=unicef.cn|publisher=UNFPA; UNICEF}}</ref>

===2000===
Infant mortality rates are based on the [[Fifth National Population Census of the People's Republic of China|5th National Population Census]] held in 2000 and calculations of male/female differences are from the medical journal article "Gender Difference of Infant Mortality and its Disparity among Provinces in China" published in the ''Chinese Journal of Health Statistics'' in April 2013.<ref name="fudanstudy"/>
